caption: Research and audit evidence. Findings are reported by the sources and have not been independently reproduced in this review.
rows: Kellas AD et al. [1]
Generates and enforces library-specific policies for pickle reconstruction.
Does not establish absence of weight backdoors or denial of service; benign compatibility is separately assessed.
Digregorio G et al. [2]
Analyzes frameworks, hubs, security-oriented loading mechanisms and user perceptions.
Reported weaknesses concern inspected versions; a secure-looking format or API name is not an end-to-end assurance claim.
Liu T et al. [3]
Maps loading paths, exception-directed bypasses and callable gadgets.
Demonstrates studied blind spots rather than a permanent claim about every current scanner release.
Applegate J et al. [4]
Uses differential fuzzing to find discrepancies between pickle implementations.
Parser agreement is distinct from an adequate policy over allowed operations.
Pastore F et al. [5]
Places model exchange inside the federated-learning trust boundary.
Keeping training records local does not by itself constrain artifact reconstruction or model execution.
Zhu R et al. [6]
Studies persistent TensorFlow APIs and model-embedded operational capabilities.
Avoiding pickle does not remove effects available through graph operations; results are framework/version specific.
Dahlgren F et al. [7]
Audits the safetensors implementation and reviews fixes.
Historical findings must be read with the fix review; they are not evidence that the same issues remain in current releases.

caption: Documented control boundaries. Entries describe specified versions or retrieval snapshots, not a safety ranking or an independent product evaluation.
rows: Python pickle [8]
General object reconstruction; documentation warns against untrusted input.
Reconstruction permissions and trusted source assumptions.
PyTorch weights-only [9,10]
Restricted reconstruction under documented version/call conditions.
Allowed-type changes, architecture code and execution environment.
Keras model loading [11]
safe_mode is documented for unsafe lambda handling and particular format applicability.
Other reconstruction behavior and the exact installed implementation.
TensorFlow graphs [12]
Graph representation executed as a program.
Permitted operations and process capabilities.
Safetensors [7,13]
Header plus tensor data; constrained representation and validation requirements.
Parser implementation, model architecture and runtime behavior.
ONNX external data [14]
Tensor bytes can be referenced outside the primary model file.
Referenced objects, resolution policy and consuming runtime.
GGUF [15]
Typed metadata and tensor storage with quantization information.
Native parsing, consumer implementation and runtime interpretation.
scikit-learn / skops [16,17]
Persistence selection and review of untrusted object types.
User approvals, compatible environment and effective type policy.
NumPy arrays [18]
Object arrays use pickle; documented default disallows it.
Actual array kind, caller setting and time of materialization.
Hub / remote modeling code [19,20]
Source identity, artifact scanning and remote-code review.
Authentic does not imply benign; selected code is separate from tensor bytes.
Static/runtime scanners [21-24]
Analyzer findings, invocation outcomes and hook scope differ.
Unsupported input, scan failure, context lifetime and unmediated routes.

caption: Proposed admission record. This is reporting guidance derived from the synthesis, not an operationally validated standard.
rows: Object identity
Digests, packaging, selected repository revision and referenced objects.
The inspected object is the one selected for consumption.
Consumer route
Framework version, API, arguments, parser/container selection and custom code.
The analyzed representation matches the consuming path.
Inspection outcome
Completed, finding, review item, unsupported route or error; wrapper response.
No detection is distinguished from no successful analysis.
Reconstruction policy
Allowed types/callables, explicit approvals and changes made for compatibility.
The consumed policy is the policy that was assessed.
Activation scope
Entry points and lifetime of runtime checks; later materialization operations.
Relevant actions are mediated when they actually occur.
Runtime authority
Accessible files, network, credentials, custom operators and intended model effects.
Containment is separate from task correctness.
Reassessment trigger
Changed bytes, code, library version, policy or environment.
An earlier decision is not silently reused for a different loading configuration.
